correctness.rationale: The published quasisolution theorem identifies every \(\sigma_{2,2}\) pair with consecutive chain terms. The recurrence gives \(\Phi_3(t_k)=t_{k-1}t_{k+1}\), and consecutive terms are coprime, reducing the target gcd to \(\gcd(t_i,t_{i+3})\). Any common prime other than \(3\) satisfies \(4t_{i+1}\equiv1\), so substitution into \(t_{i+1}^2+t_{i+1}+1\equiv0\) forces that prime to divide \(21\), hence it is \(7\). Separate congruence arguments exclude common factors \(9\) and \(49\). Complete periods modulo \(3\) and \(7\) give the exact index conditions.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact structural invariant for the same \(\sigma_{2,2}\) pairs that the primary paper identifies as a major obstruction in odd-perfect-number arguments. It isolates all shared prime support of the two relevant cyclotomic values to \(3\) and \(7\), with exact chain-index criteria and a sharp universal bound \(21\). This is directly motivated by the source's squarefreeness conjecture and remains meaningful beyond the finite search range of currently known prime pairs.
